case_title: Pulicherla Nagaraju alias Nagaraja Reddy v. State of A.P.
ratio_decidendi: To ascertain whether an intention to cause death existed under Section 300, the Court must examine factors including: (1) nature and weapon used; (2) whether weapon was carried or found at the spot; (3) whether blow was aimed at a vital part; (4) amount of force applied; (5) whether it was in the course of a sudden quarrel; and (6) whether accused took undue advantage. Where death is caused in a sudden quarrel with a single blow without premeditation, the conviction is properly under Section 304 Part II rather than Section 302.

case_title: State of Andhra Pradesh v. Rayavarapu Punnayya
ratio_decidendi: Established the definitive three-stage test to distinguish culpable homicide (Section 299) from murder (Section 300). Culpable homicide is the genus, and murder is the species. All murder is culpable homicide, but not vice-versa. Clause 3 of Section 300 requires proof of objective bodily injury intended to be inflicted, and subjective medical probability that such injury is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.

case_title: Ghapoo Yadav and Others v. State of M.P.
ratio_decidendi: Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC requires four cumulative ingredients: (i) sudden fight; (ii) absence of premeditation; (iii) act done in the heat of passion; and (iv) the offender not having taken undue advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner. Time elapsed between provocation and act determines whether passion had cooled.

case_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
ratio_decidendi: Arrest should not be automatic in offences punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years. Police officers must apply Section 41 CrPC checklist and record reasons before arrest. Directs judicial magistrates not to authorize detention mechanically in Tier 1 and Tier 2 penal offences.

case_title: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
ratio_decidendi: Enumerated seven illustrative categories where High Court can exercise inherent power under Section 482 CrPC to quash FIR: including where allegations taken at face value do not prima facie constitute any offence, or where the criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and constitutes a civil breach of contract.

case_title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation
ratio_decidendi: Classified offences into four distinct categories (A to D) for bail adjudication: Category A covers offences punishable up to 7 years (routine bail without arrest); Category B covers offences punishable with life imprisonment or death; Category C covers Special Acts (NDPS, PMLA); Category D covers economic offences. Reasserted that bail is the rule and jail is the exception.

Distinguished 'common intention' under Section 34 from 'similar intention'. Common intention implies a pre-arranged plan and acting in concert in pursuant of that plan. Prior meeting of minds, even if formed on the spot, is an indispensable prerequisite before vicarious joint liability attaches.
